topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: Stepping into the old house, the air is thick with memories. Each creak of the floorboards whispers stories only the walls could know. My sibling and I wander through rooms that hold echoes of our childhood summers, the scent of my grandmother’s lavender sachets lingering in the drawers. We find treasures hidden in the corners—forgotten photographs, a basket of half-faded letters, a quilt folded neatly at the foot of the bed. It’s more than just a house; it’s a vessel of time, each corner cradling pieces of our family’s past. As we sort through the years, we’re not just inheriting a home, but a legacy of warmth and belonging.
